long_biography.plain_text:
A visit to a Taiwanese competitor gave Volex's Nat Rothschild a practical benchmark for the factories he led. The rival's manufacturing methods impressed him, even though its profitability lagged behind his own company's. He made the exchange of production knowledge between plants a central part of his approach to running the electrical manufacturer.

After becoming operationally involved in 2015, Rothschild brought in a specialist to lead continuous improvement, initially as a consultant and later as a full-time employee. Teams shared methods developed at their most advanced factories across countries and continents. He also invested in making more components internally, including cable extrusion and electric-vehicle charging products, where production volumes justified the investment.
